title: Merged remote code branches and recorded orphan processes are removed only by an operator command
goal: backlog.py tidy --remote lists each code/<id> branch on origin whose commits git cherry finds on origin/main; no tidy run, land, close or SessionStart deletes a remote branch (the operator's g-remote answer), so a merged code branch is removed only by the operator's own command; tidy --class process lists each process an own record names, removable only when its recorded session's coord lease is gone and its start time matches the record; --apply ends those with SIGTERM, then SIGKILL after END_WAIT_S, refused in an agent session; a process no record names is listed and never signalled

run:
import sys
def _fail(t, e, tb, _d=sys.excepthook):
    if issubclass(t, AssertionError):
        print("check failed:", e); sys.exit(1)
    _d(t, e, tb)
sys.excepthook = _fail
import os, subprocess, sys, tempfile, json, time
T = tempfile.mkdtemp()
ENV = {k: v for k, v in os.environ.items() if not k.startswith(("GIT_", "KB_COORD"))}
ENV.pop("CLAUDECODE", None)
ENV.update(KB_COORD_STORE=os.path.join(T, "coord.sqlite"), GIT_CONFIG_GLOBAL=os.devnull, GIT_CONFIG_NOSYSTEM="1",
           GIT_AUTHOR_NAME="t", GIT_AUTHOR_EMAIL="t@example.com", GIT_COMMITTER_NAME="t", GIT_COMMITTER_EMAIL="t@example.com")
def g(*a, cwd):
    return subprocess.run(["git", *a], cwd=cwd, env=ENV, capture_output=True, text=True, check=True).stdout
def tool(*a, env=None, ok=(0,)):
    r = subprocess.run([sys.executable, *a], capture_output=True, text=True, env=env or ENV, timeout=300)
    assert r.returncode in ok, (a, r.returncode, r.stdout[-800:], r.stderr[-800:])
    return r
O, C = os.path.join(T, "origin.git"), os.path.join(T, "clone")
g("init", "-q", "--bare", "-b", "main", O, cwd=T)
g("clone", "-q", O, C, cwd=T)
os.makedirs(os.path.join(C, "kb", "_self", "backlog"))
open(os.path.join(C, "backlog.json"), "w").write('{"item_dir": "kb/_self/backlog"}\n')
open(os.path.join(C, "kb", "_self", "backlog", ".keep"), "w").close()
g("add", "-A", cwd=C); g("commit", "-qm", "base", cwd=C); g("push", "-q", "origin", "main", cwd=C); g("fetch", "-q", cwd=C)
WT = os.path.join(C, ".claude", "worktrees")
def wt(name, branch=None, at="HEAD"):
    p = os.path.join(WT, name)
    g("worktree", "add", "-q", *(["-b", branch] if branch else ["--detach"]), p, at, cwd=C)
    return p
n = lambda p: os.path.normcase(os.path.realpath(p))
def own(p, cls, *a, env=None):
    return tool("_tools/backlog.py", "--root", C, "own", str(p), "--class", cls, *a, env=env)
def rows(*a):
    return json.loads(tool("_tools/backlog.py", "--root", C, "tidy", "--json", *a).stdout)
def by_path(rs, cls=None):
    return {n(x["path"]): x for x in rs if "path" in x and (cls is None or x.get("class") == cls)}
def push(*a, cwd=C): g("push", "-q", "origin", *a, cwd=cwd)
push("HEAD:refs/heads/code/ST-aaaaaaaa")
x = wt("agent-x", "tmp-x"); open(os.path.join(x, "f.txt"), "w").write("x"); g("add", "f.txt", cwd=x); g("commit", "-qm", "unmerged", cwd=x)
push("HEAD:refs/heads/code/ST-bbbbbbbb", cwd=x)
g("fetch", "-q", "origin", cwd=C)
remote = lambda: g("ls-remote", "origin", "refs/heads/code/*", cwd=C)
r = tool("_tools/backlog.py", "--root", C, "tidy", "--remote")
assert "code/ST-aaaaaaaa" in r.stdout, ("the merged code branch is not listed", r.stdout)
assert "code/ST-bbbbbbbb" not in r.stdout, ("an unmerged code branch is listed as merged", r.stdout)
before = remote()
agent = dict(ENV, CLAUDECODE="1")
for env in (agent, ENV):
    tool("_tools/backlog.py", "--root", C, "tidy", "--remote", "--apply", env=env, ok=(0, 2))
    assert remote() == before, ("tidy deleted a remote branch", remote())
for env in (agent, ENV):
    tool("_tools/backlog.py", "--root", C, "tidy", "--apply", "--older-than", "0", env=env, ok=(0, 1, 2))
    assert remote() == before, ("tidy --apply deleted a remote branch", remote())

gates.question: Who deletes merged code/<id> branches on origin (846 today, all merged), and should the forge delete them itself on merge?
options: operator command only: tidy --remote --apply from the operator's own terminal, merged-only, refused in agent sessions; and the operator changes the forge's code/* protection so a merge deletes its own source branch, once the research story confirms that protection as the cause
operator command only, forge settings unchanged
no remote deletion: tidy only counts them
gates.recommendation: operator command only: tidy --remote --apply from the operator's own terminal, merged-only, refused in agent sessions; and the operator changes the forge's code/* protection so a merge deletes its own source branch, once the research story confirms that protection as the cause
gates.answer: no remote deletion: tidy only counts them

gates.question: May tidy end processes? (Today a live detached headless worker shows in procs as an orphan with parent 1, so parent 1 is no proof.)
options: end only a process an own record names whose recorded session's coord lease is gone and whose start time matches the record, by an operator run outside agent sessions; every other process is reported only (backlog.py procs)
report only: the operator ends processes by hand
gates.recommendation: end only a process an own record names whose recorded session's coord lease is gone and whose start time matches the record, by an operator run outside agent sessions; every other process is reported only (backlog.py procs)
gates.answer: end only a process an own record names whose recorded session's coord lease is gone and whose start time matches the record, by an operator run outside agent sessions; every other process is reported only (backlog.py procs)

gates.question: Where do process rows show: only under tidy --class process, or in every tidy run (and the SessionStart report)?

gates.recommendation: only under tidy --class process (other runs, --report and the SessionStart line are unchanged)

gates.question: How does tidy --remote read the remote: remote-tracking refs as last fetched, or a fresh fetch or ls-remote?
options: remote-tracking refs as last fetched (offline), lists the merged branches and counts the others; --apply, --report and --class with it exit 2
gates.recommendation: remote-tracking refs as last fetched (offline), lists the merged branches and counts the others; --apply, --report and --class with it exit 2

gates.question: Which recorded processes does tidy keep, and which go with their record alone?
options: keep one whose record has no session or no start time, or whose start time differs more than 2 s; a recorded process that no longer runs goes with its record alone, no signal
keep every recorded process whose record lacks a session, and also every one not running
gates.recommendation: keep one whose record has no session or no start time, or whose start time differs more than 2 s; a recorded process that no longer runs goes with its record alone, no signal

notes: Test policy (D-6kei5o2z, D-2tq4fhgs): no new test or test file; the checks are tool runs on a throwaway clone with planted inputs (KB_COORD_STORE points at its own coord store, so no check writes the clone's real one); no change to _tools/tests_ceiling.json. Never kill by pattern (a host hook blocks pkill -f). Premise (2026-10-19): backlog.py procs names 3 orphans, one a gk MCP server orphaned 4 days in review-j65ihctq, and one a live detached headless worker (claude, parent 1, in agent-ST-xlxkap7l): parent 1 is no proof a process is finished. The 846 origin code/* branches remain although every request is sent with merge_request.remove_source_branch (kg_sync.push_options; request !1247 merged with force_remove_source_branch true): code/* is a protected branch pattern on the forge, a likely cause the research story confirms. Reworded 2026-10-20 to the operator's g-remote answer (no remote deletion: tidy only counts them): goal clauses 1-2 and check 0 no longer ask tidy --remote --apply to delete; check 0 asserts that no tidy run deletes a remote branch, in an agent session or not.
